key_big: A square is n × n; a cube is n × n × n
key_sub: Square roots and cube roots undo them.
body_html:
How it works

A perfect square is a number like 49 = 7². A perfect square never ends in 2, 3, 7 or 8, and the sum of the first n odd numbers is n².

A perfect cube is a number like 125 = 5³. To find a root by prime factorisation, group the prime factors in pairs (square root) or triples (cube root) and take one from each group.

Example

Find √1,764 by prime factorisation.

1,764 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 × 7

Take one from each pair: 2 × 3 × 7

Answer: 42

Example

What is the smallest number to multiply 72 by to make a perfect square?

72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

One 2 has no partner

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

  • Working out 7² as 7 × 2 = 14.
  • Halving a number instead of taking its square root (√64 is 8, not 32).
  • Writing 4³ as 12 instead of 4 × 4 × 4 = 64.

faq.q: Which digits can a perfect square end in?
faq.a: 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9. A number ending in 2, 3, 7 or 8 is never a perfect square.

faq.q: How do you find a cube root by prime factorisation?
faq.a: Write the number as a product of primes, group equal primes in threes and multiply one prime from each group.

items.q: Between which two whole numbers is √96?

items.q: Between which two whole numbers is √111?
